classification_rule_pinned_before_runnin.monotone: not flat, and the excess sequence is weakly non-increasing or non-decreasing
classification_rule_pinned_before_runnin.usable_step: a declared step with a reading whose r >= 10 (the pre-declared floor)
classification_rule_pinned_before_runnin.the_multiplier_is_a_convention: 2.0 is not derived from anything. It is the ordinary default, chosen in advance because choosing in advance is worth more than choosing well. The sensitivity below makes the arbitrariness visible instead of merely confessed.

gap_no_region_records.meaning: a DECLARED ramp step at which no region was produced at all. Distinct from a combination-level absence, where the step produced a region but this (region, flavour) has no reading — those are listed per trajectory under `absent_positions_no_reading_for_this_combination` and carry NO recorded per-step reason, which is why they are named separately rather than pooled.

steps.reason: every instance at this ramp step yielded a region too small to blend (r < m) or empty. The step is recorded as a GAP and is never interpolated over.

gaps_are_drawn_never_interpolated: a declared ramp step with no reading is held as an explicit null in `excess_by_step` and listed in `gap_positions_no_region`; plot lines BREAK at it rather than bridging it. An absent reading is a claim of continuity unless the absence is itself recorded.
controls_redrawn_per_step: VERIFIED, not assumed: controls are matched on r and r moves along the ramp, so a reused control would show an identical (mean, sd) pair at two different r. No such pair exists among non-degenerate controls.

degenerate_control_profiles.label: INSUFFICIENT-degenerate (the v3 spec's own pre-declared vocabulary)
degenerate_control_profiles.what: control SD is exactly 0 because every control draw violated — the profile saturates at (1.0, 0.0). Such a control has no signature to compare, so it is excluded from the reuse detector rather than flagged by it. Every instance sits at small r under `minority`, where a random subset almost never survives a 3-way XOR.

plot_coverage.note: drawn as small multiples — one panel per (row, region) — so every trajectory in the family appears. No cap, nothing dropped.
